mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns do not deviate significantly (more than ±0.5%) from the prior month's average when the trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return, reflecting optimism about labor market strength.
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive months with such an increase, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the mean of non-trigger months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO contraction of more than 2% signals supply-side weakness, which is expected to depress corporate earnings growth and produce negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During three consecutive contraction months, the 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative deviation from the pre-contraction average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 10% above its prior month, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating stronger consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
failure_condition: Across 5 such events, the average 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than the average of non-trigger periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as lower real rates incentivize investment in equities.
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE remains below 4% for >6 months, the 60-day forward returns do not outperform the 20-day average over the prior year (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in RSAFS (retail sales) exceeds +20% from the prior month, it indicates accelerating consumer spending, which is expected to drive a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the mean of non-accelerating months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of GDPC1 (GDP) above 2% growth and INDPRO contraction of >1% in the same month predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return due to conflicting demand-supply signals.
failure_condition: During 5 such co-occurring events, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly worse than the average of non-co-occurring months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where CPIAUCSL (inflation) exceeds 3% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative as investors anticipate rate hikes and devalue equities.
failure_condition: During such inflation episodes, the 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative deviation from the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05).
